utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Saxon, you're standing with an object in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. A brief procedural point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Last evening, when the Prosecution was reviewing the transcripts of yesterday's testimony, the Prosecution realised that it made an error yesterday, in that at lines 4 through 20 on page 2698 of the transcript, the Prosecution questioned this witness about a subject matter which the witness had discussed with the Prosecution during proofing of the witness. However, the Prosecution inadvertently omitted to include this subject matter in its proofing note or notes to the Defence; and, therefore, the Prosecution became concerned that it had improperly led evidence that it should not have. The Prosecution and the Defence counsel spoke last evening, and the Defence counsel have told the Prosecution they do not feel prejudiced by this, and they wish that the lines of testimony remain in the record as they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. We had understood that there was going to be a short period before the witness came into court, when more than one procedural matter could be dealt with. The witness is here. I think in view of that, it might be preferable, Mr. Apostolski, if we left it until later in the day to hear from you on another matter. Mr. Hutsch, good morning. I again remind you that the affirmation you made still applies to your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, before we begin today, I would like to remind both you and myself that we need to speak slowly, and we need to pause between questions and answers; all right? Before we return to the notes that we were looking at yesterday, I'd like to go back just briefly to some observations that you had made on the morning of 12th of August at that first observation point. You mentioned yesterday that you saw, through binoculars, a Hermelin vehicle, a Hermelin APC. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you notice any particular markings on that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This vehicle is coloured in a green, and there were the badges with "PM" on the sides of this Hermelin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the letters "PM," what did that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Policia Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At any time around that time when you noticed the Hermelin APC, did you happen to observe any other armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess there were another BTR APC in this area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What is a BTR?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: BTR, it's an APC for eight up to ten persons, with a top pick and a 14.5 machine-gun inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Inside it or on it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: On it, in this top pick, in this tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what markings, if any, did you notice on this BTR armoured personnel carrier?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These BTRs were coloured like the normal army APCs; and if they were used by the police, they had these badges also on the sides and on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did the badges say?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "PM," Policia Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And during this time earlier the morning when you were making these observations and you observed two groups of policemen going towards Ljuboten village, did you observe, if I can put it this way, any normal vehicles; that is, vehicles that were not armoured?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some -- some police Jeeps around in the area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "there were police Jeeps around in the area"; where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This column in the north was followed by a Cherokee Jeep, a white Cherokee Jeep, with the blue lights of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And any other markings on this Jeep, this white Cherokee Jeep?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As well, this normal sticker from the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you can turn now, please, back to tab 11 in your binder, which is again Rule 65 ter number 167. Yesterday, we started looking at the notes that you wrote on the morning of the 12th of August, and we stopped after discussing the notes. Effectively, it's the first series of notes. It has ERN Number -- well, what we discussed yesterday began with the words: "Telephone, N. Beqiri, at 0740 hours." Can you turn the page, please, to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if, on e-court, we could go to the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, the next page begins with the words: "0803." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were you noting down on this page?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was noting down there what I told you some minutes before, and yesterday as well, that we had two columns. In the north, a column that was supported by APCs; and in the south, they were attacking around this Hill 631. And that the attack in the north, that is my suppose, my imagination, my vision, is going into the direction of Ljuboten and direction of the centre and the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to go a little bit more slowly, the second line of this page, we see the words: "MUP attack." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the term "MUP" in your notes, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the -- the normal abbreviation under the journalists for riot police, and, yeah, we were just using that through all the Balkan conflict that we called just in referring to the Yugoslavian police. We were calling them MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in this context, does "MUP" refer to Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, after the first few notes, we see the words: "Info, Carsten telephone, 0820 hours." Who is Carsten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the correspondent of the news agency DPR, that's the German news agency, Deutsche Presse Agentur. And he was the correspondent, Balkan correspondent, and he was at this time in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you give us the last name of Carsten, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Carsten Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below the lines that say: "Carsten, telephone," was this information you noted down provided by Carsten? Was there a telephone call with Carsten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. We had a phone call at 8.20, and I told Carsten what was going on in Ljuboten or in Ljubanci, between the villages, and Carsten told me that what is written under this -- this line: "Carsten telephone."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first line there says: "MUP attack on direct orders of B.," just a capital B there. Do you know or do you recall was referred to by this capital B?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the former Minister of Interior, Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, there's some language. It says: "Conflict between Ministry of Defence, Ministry of the Interior, about conduct," and then it says: "No NLA in LJU." What does LJU stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: LJU stands for "Ljuboten."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So these notes here is information relayed to you by Carsten Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. But I have to correct this translation. "V.M." Stands for Minister of Defence, not for "ministry," and "IM," it's the abbreviation for Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Not Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we turn to the next page, please? The next page begins with the line: "No fire from Ljuboten - 0827 hours." Then below, it says: "Spearheads enter Ljuboten." Below that we see: "Explosions, detonation flash south of orthodox church. Intense AK-fire." "AK-fire," what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "MG-fire" means machine-gun fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And "AK-fire," what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "AK," is AK-47. That's means the abbreviation for Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that it says: "Northwest town periphery. Individual RPG fire." "RPG," does that stand for rocket-propelled grenade?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at 08.34, below that, we see there's a note about the roof of the house that the entry to town is on fire." Were these observations then that you made?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I would ask that these notes be marked for identification. I'm going to come back to them later, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P308, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, yesterday you described how, apart from making notes in your notebook, you had another method of recording information at this time. You described how you used a map of the area, and on that map you placed a plastic sheet; and then you described how you made notes with a waterproof pen on that plastic sheet; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like you to look now, please, at what is tab 9 in your binder -- actually, I apologise. Tab 10, please. Tab 10, which is an enlargement of the map that is in tab 9. Tab 9 is 65 ter number 1027. Tab 10, you see the map that's there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That is the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. I want you to look at the map. It should be a map.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's tab 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise. It's in tab 9, then.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And is this map, that is provided for you in tab 9, is this sort of a more focused version of the map that you used?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see I'm causing some confusion with the Defence, so I'm going to go more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're grateful to the Prosecution. I don't think there is any confusion, but the wrong documents appear to be on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. If we could start with tab 9, please. It's my fault. Tab 9, which is 65 ter 1027.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, please take a look at the map on the screen in front of you. Is this a copy of the map that you used to make your markings on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe in your binder, at tab 9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, it would be simplest, Your Honour, if this map could be tendered into evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To make things easier to understand, the Prosecution has produced a version of this map that focuses more directly on the areas of Ljubanci. Do you see that map in your binder at tab 9?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher's assistance, please, to place this map on the ELMO. And if I could ask the assistance of the audio-visual people, if the projector could be as high as possible, please, so we can see more of the map. Maybe that's it. There we go. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Hutsch, I have a question for you just so that we understand the work that you did. On the left-hand side of the map, we see, in a vertical line every couple of centimetres, some black numbers. They start towards the top at 65, and they go down 64, 63, 62. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then we also see, going horizontally in the center of the map, we see some black numbers, 31, 32, 33, 34. Do you see those numbers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you began to make notes on a plastic sheet, how did you use those numbers to assist you or those grids, if I can say it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used just a crossing of these grids to fix my plastic overlay so that afterwards, when I had to take away the plastic overlay, I can find it on every map with the same grid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And where did you fix your plastic sheet, at what coordinates on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you can turn now, you should have also in tab 10 some copies of plastic sheets. And this would be 65 ter number, we'll start with, 385, and this plastic sheet has an ERN number N003-0002. Mr. Hutsch, could you take that plastic sheet that was in tab 11, the first one, and place it on the map the way you did it on early in the morning of Sunday, the 12th of August, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I'd like to provide you with a copy -- a hard copy of the image that you now see on your screen. The Prosecution was able to produce them yesterday, and the Defence has copies. If I could ask the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Hutsch, you've now placed the plastic sheet on the map using the grid coordinates 33-64 as a marker. Can you tell us, please, perhaps starting at the top, there is an arrow sort of at the top of the map, towards the center. There's an arrow pointing up and the letters or word "BRODE." Below that, it says "VVD," and below that, I believe it says "TEE1." What were you recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was recording that in Brodec - I think I've got something lost with the hole for the binder - so the last word, so we were talking about Brodec. Brodec is a village, but I see here it's 500 metres more of this arrow. And, in this village, there were located parts of a logistical centre or logistical unit and parts of 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 1st Company of what?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 3rd Battalion, 1st Guardist Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Of the Army of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If we could move downwards, please, towards the center of the map, and perhaps you could use that high-tech pointer that you just had in your hands to indicate to the Judges what you're speaking about. Can you slowly describe, there are some letters that say -- appear to say: "T" - I'm not sure what the next letter is - it says: "1", and below that it says: "MUP," and then there are some markings. What are you recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here [Indicates], it's just the German abbreviation for Tyler."Tyler" means parts, parts of the 1st Company, 3rd Battalion, 1st Guardist Brigade of the Army of Macedonia, and they are in partly positions in Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness is pointing to some blue lines on the map to the right of the number "1."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see the abbreviation: "MUP." What were you recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the assembly area, the attack starting position of police forces. That means they are located in Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see the letters: "AB" and then: "10.8"; and below that, we see a horizontal line and a figure that I could really describe. Can you tell us what you were noting there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the tactical -- tactical sign for mortars that seemed to be there, and the word "Up" means "since." And then we have the "10th of August," and that means parts of this police forces are there since the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then moving to the right now, first, we see a blue line going, if I say -- no, no, Mr. Hutsch. Let me guide you. All right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mmm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a short blue line going from southwest, curving toward the northeast, through the word "Ljubanci." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then to the right of that, we see a similar line, but it's black. And at the top of that line, we see the letters "AL." And to the right of that black line, we see two arrows. Can you tell us what information you were recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a coordination line that every tactical operational leader needs to coordinate an attack. So this is a so-called attack line. And because I monitored the first incidents in this area around -- at 8.00 and three minutes, and that's an unusual time for an attack. Normally, a leader would give a clear attack time. That would mean -- and this meant for me that the first spearheads had to cross this line at 8.00. That's what I was writing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What do those two arrows depict?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two arrows shows the two groups: The northern attack group of police forces and the southern attack group of police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And those two arrows indicate movement towards the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And the word "Ljuboten" is partly blocked by a circle, but there's a circle there; and, inside the circle, we see the number "22". What were you recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the number "22." It's the capital for " ZZ." That means it's a part target of the attack. That means a leader has to give his forces an objective and a target that they have to possess or they had to conquer, doing something with them. And to make it much more easier to coordinate fire and movement, he has to give them part targets on their way to this main target. And for me, it was clear that this target with "ZZ" is the part target for this police forces that was around the mosque in Ljuboten. So it was clearly to see by everybody because of the minarets, and it was clear that you could defend it easily if you would have riot spread there. And on the third, you are able to give their logistical support to the attacking troops or to reinforce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We also see now, above the village of Ljuboten, just above it, there is a blue line, and it goes from the northwest towards the southeast. And underneath the blue line, we see the letters "61008." Can you tell us what you were depicting in this first blue line?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first blue line is showing the area that is covered by the 2nd Company, 3rd Battalion, 1st Guardist Brigade from the Army. These numbers are belonging to this circle. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Hutsch. The numbers 61008, those numbers refer to the circle with the letters "ZZ" inside it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, with the other one, the blue line, the first one. That means that was a target area for artillery/mortars, and we have impacts in this area between 6.00 and 10.00 and eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Close to that blue line that you described a minute ago, there is sort of an oval-shaped red circle, if I can describe it, and then there's a blue line leading vertically down through the village of Rastak and down to the village of Camorrista. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then there's a triangle or a question mark to the right of that oval. What were you trying to depict here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So first the blue line partly west of Rastak are positions -- are the area that is covered by the 3rd Company, 3rd Battalion, 1st Guardist Brigade of the Army; and in the northern part that is circled with red, we have mortar fire that is fired by the NLA at 5.00 and 12 minutes in the afternoon. So here we have had impacts; and the triangle means that in my point of view, the NLA had a forward observer to lead the mortar fire into this area, but I was not sure. So every information that was not confirmed is marked with a question mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just for the record, that question mark is just to the left of the number 60; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, just to make sure that the record is clear, this oval-shaped red circle, which you said -- I just want to be clear. Is it your evidence that this circle represents the area where NLA artillery or mortar fire shells were landing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Hutsch, if we move down a bit to the northeast -- excuse me, the southeast, we see what looks a bit like a blue lightning bolt. We see arrows at both ends. Can you tell us, please, what you were depicting there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a position for reconnaissance that is done by the army between the single villages on the western or southwestern part of the mountain and forested area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "reconnaissance done by the army," which army are you speaking about?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If we can now direct your attention up, vertically up on the map, sort of near the -- going towards the northeast corner of the map, there is a number "62" in black, bold letters; and around that number -- to the right of that number, "62," there are a number of markings, some letters, and some numbers. Can you tell us, please, what information you were recording there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm recording there that the NLA is doing some reconnaissance since 2.00 in the afternoon towards Ljuboten, that they build up a mortar position with 60- up to 82-millimetre mortars from the NLA Brigade 114 in this area. [Indicates] And that from 5.00 in the afternoon on, reconnaissance is forwarded to Ljuboten from the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does that mean -- what do you mean when you say "reconnaissance is forwarded to Ljuboten" or "NLA reconnaissance forwarded to Ljuboten"? Can you be a bit clearer?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that -- that the leader of this reconnaissance troop gets the order to go into Ljuboten and to see what is going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you see your red arrows there going from the northeast towards the southwest, those red arrows are pointing, if I can say this, sort of down the mountains towards the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do those red arrows indicate that members of the NLA reached the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That means that they are just doing their reconnaissance in the direction of Ljuboten, but they've not already entered Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, again, this information that you marked on this plastic sheet, you -- this was information that you recorded from your observations?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recorded the information -- this information. [Indicates] I recorded from my own observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has just indicated with a circle the information on this map around the villages of Ljubanci and Ljuboten in black and blue letters -- in black and blue ink.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The information from -- about the placement of parts of the army in Brodec were done by telephone investigation. What I saw is the -- what I monitored were just the fire, when the rounds were fired in this area. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For the record, you're indicating now the information related to the NLA; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the mortar position, I suppose that has been in this area [Indicates] because I saw the start -- when the mortar grenades are put into the mortar and it explodes, then you have a long fireball, and you can see that. That's what I saw, as well as I saw the impacts in the area of Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And your information about NLA reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These information were given by Nazim Beqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Via telephone?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via telephone, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender this image with ERN N002-0002 with map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You say "with map." You want the hard copy or the image? It's the image you're thinking of, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. That will be received as two parts of the one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour. I apologise. Simply for the record, we would make the same indication as we did yesterday in relation to the previous map and drawing made by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn now to what is tab 15 in your binder, Mr. Hutsch, and this is Rule 65 ter number 176. It's ERN number N001-7280. Mr. Hutsch, do you see this panoramic photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise to the Court Officer. I've made a mistake. I should have said 65 ter number 176 at tab 15. It may simply be the next item in this ERN range. No, there it is. There it is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, did you produce the annotations on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What view do we have now in this photograph? In other words, from what direction towards what direction?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a view from north to south.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so if you can describe, please, it says: "Mortar rounds" on the right-hand side in blue letters: "0800", and then we see two arrows in blue: One has the word "South" underneath it. The other has the word "North" underneath it. Can you tell me what those arrows show?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two arrows show the two attack groups: The first in the north entering the eastern part -- sorry, the western part of Ljuboten, and the southern group that was surrounding Hill 631.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So that southern group, you were able to follow their progress because it wasn't blocked by Hill 631; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. In the -- towards the middle of the photograph, we see a black circle with an arrow leading up to "Impacts 0711." What are you depicting here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are impacts, mortar impacts that we were told that were in this area at 7.00 and 11 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then moving toward the left of this photograph, which I guess would be moving from west to east, we see a large arrow in broken lines. Do you see that, in blue?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there's a word "North" underneath the photograph pointing to the arrow. What were you depicting here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the future progress of the attack from the northern attacking group, who are going -- who are attacking Ljuboten in direction of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, when you were at Observation Point 1 and Hill 631 was in front of you, were you able to follow, at that time, all of this progress of the northern group?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because the Hill 631 blocked my view on the progress completely, so I didn't see the northern group with my own eyes when they left Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you hear with relation to the northern group?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard in the area where I guessed that the northern group was attacking, that means along the street between Ljubanci and Ljuboten, I heard MG fire, Kalashnikov fire, single APG shots. And, yeah, that was -- that was what I could hear, some detonation flash.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The information on this annotated photograph, did it come from your notes?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps, instead of making the point every time, we'll indicate that our point of yesterday will apply to all of the pictures said to have been prepared or made pursuant to observation on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be received as Exhibit P311, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could look at, Mr. Hutsch, what is in tab 16 of your binder, which is again an annotated photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is an annotated photograph from the same 65 ter number 176. It has ERN number N001-7281, and this says at the top: "Sunday, 12 August 2001, progress of the attack." Did you make these annotations based on your notes, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the photograph, we see a circle in red, and there's a line going up to the words: "Destination flash," and an arrow going down to the note -- to the time "827." "Explosions," also "RPG," below that "AK-47 fire," below that "Machine-gun fire," "Roof of a house burns." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then moving towards the center of the photograph, we see a blue arrow. What does that blue arrow indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This blue arrow indicates the progress of the attack, going towards the center of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And more toward the left, we see two blue circles with arrows pointing down, and then the indication "0834, single mortar shells." What do those blue circles indicate, then?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That indicates that in this area, we have had impacts of mortar. So they were firing some -- some rounds into this areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P312, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, at some point on that Sunday morning, did you decide to change your location?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because since around 8.30, it shows me that I couldn't follow what really was going on in the field, so -- because Hill 631 was blocking my view to the incidents, what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so at that time what did you decide to do?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we decided to change our position and to look for a new point where we could follow on what was going on in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could you turn to tab 12 in your binder, please. And, Your Honours, this is a printout of a panoramic photograph from the Ljuboten panorama presentation. It has ERN number N005-7991. And perhaps with the usher's assistance, could Mr. Hutsch's copy of this large photograph be placed on the ELMO. We may need to move it a bit. And do you know what, we may have a less rumpled version, perhaps, for Mr. Hutsch. I'm grateful to Ms. Walpita for assisting me with that. And I'm wondering if the audio-visual people could switch us to the ELMO, because what I'm seeing is -- there we are. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, could you please move this photograph to the left, please. That's fine, just stop right there. And a little bit more to the left, a little bit more to the left, a little bit more -- no, Mr. Hutsch, go back the other way, please. Keep going, keep going, keep going. We see here, in the left-hand corner, capital letters "OP-2." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does this photograph depict the view that you had from the second observation point that you went to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Do you have a marker there with you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps starting on this side of the photograph, first of all, approximately what time did you reach this observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 8.45 and 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was this a better observation point for you than the first observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because as you have seen or you are seeing now, we had a close view to Ljuboten and we could follow what was going on in Ljuboten from this point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Hutsch, could you please perhaps take that marker and draw an arrow perhaps from one of those hills pointing down toward the area where the village of Ljubanci would be, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'm confused by what you just did, because that arrow is pointing out of the photograph. Do we see any of the village of Ljubanci in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see parts of the village in this area. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Will you circle that, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So that would be the eastern portion of the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could you mark a number 1 above that circle, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now moving the photograph to the right, now, if you could move the photograph towards the right. Keep going, please. Now stop there. Here are we see what is now the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you move the photograph further toward the right, please. And there on the right side, we see the mosque and the minaret; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow down to that minaret, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just write the number "2" next to that arrow.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, perhaps at this point could this photograph be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P313, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, when you came to this location between 8.45 and 9.00, did you continue to record things that you observed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you continue to record events in your notes?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we return, Your Honours, to what is now Exhibit P308, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is at tab 11 of your binder. And just for the record, the panoramic photograph that you saw a few minutes ago, the second observation point that's been marked as Exhibit P313, when you were at that position, Hill 631 was now behind you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the eastern part of Hill 631.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. All right. If you could turn now to what is the fifth page of your notes at tab 11. It is a page where the first line says: "Individual symbol, see original hits in area." And below that, we see a line that says: "Telephone Beqiri, 0917 hours." Below that, we see: "0925 hours. According to army information, no NLA in the village." Below that: "0928. Trying to find out if there are Alis as printed." Did this information come to you via the telephone?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This entry for 0928: "Trying to find out if there are Alis," can you -- and on the next page, it actually says: "If there are Alis in there," and then we see the words: "Operation supposedly only by MUP." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does this note mean: "Trying to find out if there are Alis in there"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So "Alis" was a term in referring to Ali Ahmeti, if members of the NLA are inside the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So the term "Alis" referred to members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And so then if we keep going on that page --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to my colleague, but will Mr. Saxon ask the witness where the information came from, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think we've got to the information yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understood the Prosecutor to turn to the next page, Your Honour, or to be trying to turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's fine. I believe I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This information regarding: "First no NLA in the village at 0925" and 0928: "Trying to find out if there are Alis in there," do you recall what institution this information came from?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what I can provide is that the second source, at 9.00 and 28 minutes, was a member of the UBK. That is the Intelligence of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you tell us anything about the source for the information at 0925?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This source was a member of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If we turn now to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must insist, in relation to this matter, could -- will the Prosecution ask Mr. Hutsch to identify the sources of that information? By that, I mean by their name. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry if there's lack of clarity. I thought it was clear that this witness will not identify certain sources, and I believe -- but I'll ask it for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Names to be put for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll ask it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you willing to provide us with the identities of these sources you've just referred to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not. And after I wrote -- I read an interview with Mrs. Residovic, who claimed how witnesses are to be protected and sources are to be protected, I think she will understand very well that especially in this case, I have to protect my sources, as a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can move, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we move on, perhaps a point of clarification. If the Prosecution could ask Mr. Hutsch if he is claiming that these two persons whom he refused to identify were used as sources by his work as a journalist, that may be relevant to further matters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. Hutsch was working as a journalist at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I think the question suggested is a proper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, the sources that you had at this time, were these sources of information that you used during your work as a journalist in Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can move to the entry at 0948 hours, it says: "Telephone Ejup Hamiti. They or we are trying to leave the village through the riverbed." Below that: "OSCE not allowed into village." "At 1007 hours from the Information Press Office IM," does "IM" refer to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, it says: "Ljube on his way to Ljuboten."

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Mr. Saxon has just asked the witness about the particular entry referring to the Information Press Office. Could the witness be asked or should the Prosecution perhaps ask who Mr. Hutsch says he talked to on that day in the Information Press Office of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, are you willing to provide the identity of the person in the Interior Ministry Information Press Office who provided this information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my interpreter was calling the Press Information Centre and the Ministry of the Interior, and it shouldn't be difficult for the Defence to see the duties schedules, who was on duty at this time in the press office, because it was usual just to -- to take the statements of the spokespersons. And it is usual also for journalists not to name the spokesperson with their name, so it was either for us who we spoke to. We just need the official statement from the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, can I take your response to be a "no"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't know that that follows. As I understood what Mr. Hutsch was saying, it is that he does not know who was the spokesperson for the Ministry. Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was a group of spokespersons, Your Honour, and I don't know exactly who we spoke to or my interpreter spoke to in this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Whereas, you are saying, with respect to the previous people that were contacted, you do know who were the individuals that you contacted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But you say that you are not wanting to disclose their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below the entry at 1007 hours, we see an entry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm really sorry to interject again, but this witness has indicated that the contact person within the Ministry of Interior whom he says was contacted on that day was contacted by his interpreter, and I understood that Mr. Saxon would pursue this matter so that we can identify who this interpreter is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, for the record, are you willing to provide the Chamber with the name of your interpreter or interpreters who were working with you on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not willing, because - and I think that we did all right, in the first part of my statement here - that I made clear why these interpreters would come under pressure if I would close -- disclose their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There is now an entry at 1100 hours. It says: "Explosions, RPG, machine-gun, AK-47." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This entry, was this information that came from your own observations at the second observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what were you describing here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was describing that what I saw in the area of the -- of the mosque, that I could hear some explosions, RPG, MG, Kalashnikov fire in the north part of Ljuboten, that means in the area around the monastery and the street above the -- not the monastery, the mosque, and the street above the mosque. And this fire were going slowly to south.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I stop you there, please. You use the word "fire here." By the word "fire," are you referring to flames or are you referring to something else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to -- to rifle fire and skirmish fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Gunfire?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then on that page we see: "Nine houses burning," and below that we see: "Question mark, reinforcement, approximately one platoon from Ljubanci to Ljuboten." Can you describe what you were noting down at that point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first is that all over the village from Ljubanci, I -- from Ljuboten, I was counting nine houses that were burning; and that from Ljubanci going to Ljuboten, another platoon of police officers, that means around 25 up to 30 police officers, were marching in direction to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know this group of people were police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see clearly the camouflage uniform with the police badge on the left arm and the right of Macedonia on the right arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you making these observations with binoculars?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, there's another entry: "Information Press Office, Interior Ministry," at 1123 hours. It says: "Boskoski in Ljuboten." First of all, do you know who the source of this information was?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the spokespersons in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you don't know which one?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then below that, we see, at 1150 hours, it says: "MUP," or the police, "at check-point Radu are camouflaging." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got a phone call, that means my Albanian interpreter got a phone call from an Albanian source, who told him that police officers in Radusani put masks over their face.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you willing to provide the identity of that source?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which -- which Albanian source that was, and I'm not willing to give the name of my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. To continue, we see at 1215 hours -- before we move on to 1215 hours, later on in the afternoon -- I'm going to move on. At 1215 hours, we see the notes: "14 houses burning, rifle fire waning." And then on the next page, we see the entry: "Two platoons, MUP and Hermelin, from Ljuboten direction, Ljubanci." Can you explain what you were noting there, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So at 12.15, I was counting all in all 14 houses burning. The gunfire was waning, and around 50 police officers and an unknown number of Hermelin APCs were leaving Ljuboten, that means the eastern part of Ljuboten, in direction of the western part and Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The transcript is a little bit unclear. What I see in the English transcript, it says this: "The gunfire was waning," or," or winding down, and: "Around 50 police officers in unknown number of Hermelin APCs ..." Is that what you meant to say, or can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just writing two platoons of police officers and Hermelin. So just to make it much more clear, because the phrase "platoon" may not clear for everybody, I gave the number around 50 police officers, that means two platoons. And "Hermelin," I didn't write a number before it, that means for me it was an unknown number of Hermelin, approximately one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then below that, we see, at 1300 hours the entry: "Fire weaker. Approximately 20 houses burning. Group of about 50 refugees at southern periphery of Ljuboten, direction Radu." This note about 50 so-called refugees, can you explain what you were noting down there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was around 50 inhabitants from Ljuboten leaving the village. They tried to leave the village through the -- through the small valley in direction of Radusani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were observing this through your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, at 1324 hours, there is a note related to a telephone call to Beqiri. Again, this is the person you referred to as the NLA spokesperson?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "MUP killed people in Ljuboten. At least three dead." Something at "5th Street. Boskoski in Ljuboten," and then: "Negotiations, OSCE, EU and NATO." If you can recall, what were these negotiations referring to? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazim Beqiri told us that there were some negotiations between OSCE, European Union, NATO, and the Macedonian Government that should lead to a stop of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you turn the page, actually, to the next page, we see actually that note continues. So it reads first "Negotiations" and then it says: "With Macedonian government failed. No end of attack." Is that what you wrote down in your note?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. Would this be a good time to take the first break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Saxon. We must have the first break, reconvening at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber must apologise to everybody. Another matter arose unexpectedly and which delayed us. Sorry to have kept you for waiting. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Hutsch, before we leave your notes for the time being, again just to clarify, these notes that we've looked at on pages 5 through 8 of your notes of 12 August 2001, all of these notes you made either pursuant to your own observations or information you received via telephone calls; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, when you were at Observation Point 2 on the 12th of August, did you also record information on plastic sheets, plastic overlays on a map?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If I can ask you, please, if we can move back to tab 9 in your binder, which is Prosecution Exhibit 309. Mr. Hutsch, again, this map you see in front of you, is this the map that you were working with at Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you can turn now to tab 10, please, in your binder, and, again, you should have a plastic overlay, a plastic sheet, and the A3-sized map of Ljuboten to place on the ELMO. Maybe the usher could assist you with that. Before you do that, Mr. Hutsch, did you use the same grid coordinates, I think, 33-64, to mark where you placed your plastic sheet?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both crosses are the same, I think, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, on the ELMO, can you please place that plastic sheet on the map at the same coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, to assist Your Honours, the Prosecution has created copies of the image you now see on your computer screen. The Defence have a copy, and if the usher could provide these hard copies to you, I'd be grateful. So now we see this map with the plastic overlay N003-0003 on top of it. Mr. Hutsch, tell us, please, what is the information that you've recorded on this map? Perhaps you could start with sort of a long, dark line that has the letters "AL" at one end of it.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is just the history of the skirmish. That means we have here this attacking line. [Indicates] It means the start where the police forces crossed the street in the direction of Ljuboten. We have here "12" is the day, that means the 12th of August, 8.00, and "AL," attack line. What we have in blue -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, if we could just go to the right of that line, we see two arrows, one a bit further north than the other. What do these arrows represent?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both arrows are representing the attacking groups. The northern one is showing that it is the spear point of this attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then just to the right of those heads of those arrows, we see a dotted line, and it has the numbers "0830" at the upper end of it. What are you depicting there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the line where the attack has been at 8.30, around 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then to the right of that dotted line -- first of all, towards the bottom of that dotted line, we see "0845." So does that dotted line represent events between those two time periods or no?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see "0830" at the top of that dotted line?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And towards the bottom, we see "0845." What does "0845" refer to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the advance of this position. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness is referring to a short, dark semicircle.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was reached at 8.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Above that short, dark semicircle, we see what looks like a blue dot with an arrow pointing up. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an impact area for mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe, then, what is in -- what we see in blue colour to the right of those lines?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these blue circles show impact areas of mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And the times next to those blue circles?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those show the time when these impacts went down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see one at 0607 and then another at 1018; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, by 1018, you were at Observation Point 2; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below the indication for 1018, we see another dotted line and an indication of 1220. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line [Indicates] shows the advance of the attack at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see a short, thick, dark line and the letters "1238." What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the final position of the police forces at 12.00 and 38 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, to the east of the village of Ljuboten on this map now, we see what looked like red arrows or bolts of lightning; and then further to the east, we see a small half circle and some writing in red. Can you tell us what information is recorded there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are information about the NLA. That means that we have, in this area [Indicates], a position, a fighting position of the 2nd Battalion of the 114th NLA Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you? Just for the record, the witness had been indicating a red half circle to the right of the numbers "1400." If you can continue, Mr. Hutsch, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows the two directions of reconnaissance in the north and in the south. Both reconnaissance troops had been sent out around 2.00 in the afternoon. And it shows there [Indicates] the already common-known mortar position of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, this is a red mark next to the numbers "1645."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you record this information on this map based on what you observed at Observation Points 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this map, with the plastic overlay that has N002-0003 on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, Mr. Hutsch, to what is tab 5 in your binder. I apologise, Your Honours, I misspoke. What we need to see now is the item at tab 17, which is again from 65 ter number 176, and it has the ERN number N001-7882. Mr. Hutsch, do you see this annotated photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you make these annotations?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the annotations come from your notes of the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, now, does this photograph show a view of the Ljuboten and Ljubanci area from the north, looking toward the south?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you look to the right part of the photograph first. You see a small blue circle and then an arrow pointed up, and it says: "My observation position ..." -- let me start earlier. That blue arrow, is that the -- does that indicate Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then the annotation says: "My observation position from around 1045 hours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that time correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That time is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What time, approximately, then, did you get to Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 8.45 and 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. There is a heavy black arrow going, I believe, from west to east and some annotations below it. Can you tell us -- can you describe what you were describing there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reinforcement by one platoon, that means 25 up to 30 police officers, who entered Ljuboten from Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see the words "11.00, nine houses burning," in green; and then further towards the left, we see a very rough circle in blue and then the letters: "11.00. Explosions, heavy RPG. Machine-gun, AK-47 fire." Is this information that you observed, then, from Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P315, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, briefly, can we return, please, to what is tab 12 in the binder. It is that large map that's actually on the desk in front of you -- excuse me, the large photograph, showing the view from Observation Point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, perhaps, if that could be placed again on the ELMO. For the record, it's marked for identification Exhibit P313. I'm very sorry. Perhaps, if the usher could give the version that the witness has already made some annotations on, I think that would be the best way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if you could please write on the bottom of that photograph, towards the left-hand side, the indication "0845 to 0900."

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then perhaps "12 August 2001."

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I would seek to now tender what has been marked for identification as Exhibit 313 -- P313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P313, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could turn now, please, to what is tab 18 in your binder, Mr. Hutsch. This is again from 65 ter number 176. It has ERN N001-7283. Mr. Hutsch, do you see this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At the top, it says: "PP6, Sunday - 12 August 2001" in blue letters; and below that, it says: "End of the attack." Did you make the annotations on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The information on this photograph, is this information that you observed from Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, for example, in the middle, we see the time, "12.15." And we see a heavy blue arrow, this time indicating direction from east to west. What were you indicating with this arrow?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the withdrawal from two platoons, that means around 50 police officers and a Hermelin, towards Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And above that blue arrow, we see a red circle; and then on both sides of that red circle, we see a dotted red line, one going off towards the east and the other going off towards the west. What were you depicting here with the red line?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red lines are ways of refugee groups that left Ljuboten to southeast and southwest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then toward the left of the photograph, more toward the eastern -- going toward the eastern part of Ljuboten, we see an area marked in green and an arrow pointing down. What were you trying to show with this green area?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area, around six houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, for the record, this is a view now from the north looking towards the south; right? The photograph depicts what someone would see from the north looking towards the south?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. At some point, Mr. Hutsch, after, to use your term, "the end of the attack," did you decide to leave Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I decided to leave the observation point because we had, for 30, 45 minutes, no incidents more monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And so what did you do -- approximately, when did you leave Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where did you go from Observation Point 2?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the street between Ljubanci and Radusani in direction to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you then -- was that your intended destination, Skopje, or was your intended destination somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our plan was to circle just way around, to enter the area east-southeast of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. All right. Perhaps with the usher's assistance, because we have a pen that works with that computer screen, I'd like to ask you, if you can, just roughly, to draw on the image on the computer screen the route you took to get -- to try to get close to the area of the eastern part of Ljuboten. And you can go off the photograph, if necessary. We understand that not everything can be shown on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the point where we are. [Indicates] So first we went in western direction, followed the street going to Radusani [Marks], out of the picture going to the outskirts of Skopje [Marks], did a circle for around 270 degrees, and entered this street that is leading as well to Skopje. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "this street," you just drew a red line on the upper left-hand side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that street coming close to the eastern part of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, approximately, what time did you enter that street that you just indicated with that red line?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.30, around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 1430 hours?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now seek to tender this item, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P316, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you reached that area, did you stop at some point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Around -- yes. Around two kilometres south of the Ljuboten, there was another police check-point just in a curve that leads -- if you're coming from the south, going to north, in a western direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you turn, please, to what is tab 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is from 65 ter number 199.2.21. It has N004-4579. If I could have the Court's indulgence so that I don't confuse the record. This same photograph is at page 15 of the Court binder. I'm going to ask the witness perhaps to annotate this, but first of all -- we'll wait a few minutes. It's my fault, because I wasn't clear on what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the area depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the area where the other check-point was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "the other check-point," whose check-point was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a check-point that was occupied by police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know at the time that these persons were police forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms with police badges on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you help us, please. Could you take that pen again that is attached to the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe the usher could assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could indicate with an arrow, could you point to an area where the check-point was, the police check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And for the record, above that circle that you've drawn, could you write the letters "CP" for "Check-point."
