utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can go a bit slowly, please. Did you personally drive all the way up to the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My interpreter was driving while I was sitting on the seat beneath him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you stay in the vehicle all the way up to the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this situation, for me it was -- or it seems to be much more safer to leave the car with my Macedonian-speaking language assistant, interpreter, and just to go by foot to this check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why, in your opinion at the time, was that the safest -- a safer way to approach the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, if we would just come with a car, somebody might have thought that we are doing something bad, that we are belonging, for example, to the NLA. You have to be aware that in March there was an incident in Tetovo where two members of the NLA were passing a check-point of the police. When they were stopped, they left the car and they tried to throw hand grenades into the check-point. So there were, for security reasons, good arguments to leave the car and to show there's nothing and we are just friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you refer to this incident in March in Tetovo, this is March 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: March 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. These police officers, could you tell whether they were regular police officers, reservists, or what?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I believe is that they were reserve officers, reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All of them?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the commanders have been regular officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how could you distinguish a regular police officers versus the reservist?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, the active police officers were much polite, more self-confident in their behaviour when they spoke, for example, with journalists or with other people. They seemed to be much more professional than reservist officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And was that the case when you approached this check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how these police officers were armed, if they were armed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were armed with AK-47 Kalashnikov rifles, and others just with pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you approached this check-point, apart from the police officers, did you notice any other persons present?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a group of around 30 ethnical Albanians present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how was this group of 30 ethnic Albanians dressed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was it a mixture of men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a mixture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what happened to this group of around 30 persons?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the women and children were just in the field partly south of the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you do us a favour, please. Can you take up that pen again and mark a smaller circle around the area where you saw the women and children.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And to the left of that smaller circle, could you draw the number "1," please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so then how about the ethnic Albanian men in this group, what was going on with them?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were laying on the asphalt of the road, and they were searched and beaten by these police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you personally observe this?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What, if anything, did the police officers use to beat these ethnic Albanian men?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just saw when they were using their hands and their feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. What were these police officers wearing on their feet?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers were wearing army boots and normal black shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: While this beating was going on, what, if anything, did you hear these policemen say?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They shouted to the -- to these men that they were terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what else, if anything, did you hear the police officers say? Please tell us literally.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said the translation for, "fuck your mother," so the Serbian -- the Macedonian word for that was "picka ti mater."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What observation did you make about the conditions of the men who were on the asphalt road, being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These men were highly frightened. Some of them tried to cover their body, and they were screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you observe any injuries on these men lying on the road?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some hematome [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Hematoma," is that the word?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hematoma.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And anything else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just that some blood were coming out when they were hit in their face, from their nose, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And did you notice the behaviour of a particular police officer at the time while the beating -- when the beating was going on?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the commanding officers, one was, yeah, I think, something doing like organising this scene, the scenario. So, for example, when one of these men were already searched, he was brought to a truck or to Jeeps in this area, while the other one was motivating his subordinates to beat in a right way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit clearer about that. How was this person you refer to as the commander, how was he motivating the police officers, to use your language, "to beat the persons in the right way"? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taking his -- or he was shaking his arm and showing them you have to beat in this way, and then he beat the man on the ground, himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And did that have an effect on the other police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems for me that they were beating much more harder to the men who were laying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: These ethnic Albanian men who were laying on the ground, did you notice what they were wearing on their feet?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were normal shoes and normal sports shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And while these beatings were taking place, the women and the children who were on this photograph a bit to the left of the curve in the road, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If I could ask the usher's assistance one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, could you take up that pen again that's attached to the computer and perhaps indicate, either with a circle or a line, where on the road the beatings were taking place.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them in this line. [Marks] And some also here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the first line that you drew just within that circle, could you write the number "2" above it, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on the lower line that you drew along the road, could you write the number "3" below it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this image, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, when you got to this check-point, what did you -- actually, let me go a little bit more slowly. When the beatings stopped, what happened to these men who had been beaten on the road?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have been brought to police vehicles, and these police vehicles left in direction to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How do you know these vehicles were police vehicles? How did you know?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the normal police plates on the sides, that means it's a white plate, then three numbers, then like a turned triangle; and in this triangle, it's "PM" written and, again, three numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you refer to the plate, you're referring to the license plate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you want to stop at that check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the discussion that my Macedonian interpreter had with this, I'd say, organizing police officer, we saw the chance that we could go further to Ljuboten just by handing over some presents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall what this person who appeared to be an observer or commander, did he say anything about the ethnic Albanians to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that these are terrorists, that they have been captured now, and they will be brought to prison/to court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say that you gave some presents. Can you be a little bit more specific? What present or presents did you provide to this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we provide 100 German marks; and if I remember right, we hand over also two bottles of liquor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then did you and your colleagues pass through the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you enter the village of Ljuboten then?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you started to enter the village of Ljuboten, did you continue to take notes?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We stopped already to make notes because we would like to have, in any situation, the scenario very calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so can you explain to us, help us understand, why would stopping taking notes help keep your situation calm?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are just passing by, first, it seems for somebody outside that you are just a grey mouse that nobody will pay attention to. Second, if somebody will see that you start writing something or do some photographs, he is sure that there will be a witness for that what he is doing or that somebody might have, in footsteps, an enemy purpose on him. So it is always better, if you are going into a battlefield, to stop making notes and, yeah, just to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what did you do with your notebook, then, at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We hide it in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to turn back now to what is tab 11 in your binder. This has been marked for identification as Exhibit P308, and, again, these are the notes that you took on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if the Court Officer could assist us, please, by bringing up on e-court the ninth page of these notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Here we see, on the ninth page, at 1449 hours, you wrote the following: "Group of refugees at check-point. Radu (about 30)." What does the abbreviation "Radu" stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This abbreviation is "Radusana."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Then it says: "Men must lie down on the ground, are being beaten, kicked." Then it says: "Three young men bleeding on nose, mouth, and eyebrows." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Check-point Radisani, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what we didn't have on this moment, we didn't have the time to take the grids out of the map or we hadn't the time yet to have a code name for this check-point. So it is similar in the height in the map to the other one in Radusani, which is just on the opposite side. So it was clear to us that this new check-point, we don't have a name for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say it's similar to the height, are you speaking in a topographic sense or a cartographic sense?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I inquire which?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, that may indicate, then, my poor understanding of the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you use the term "it was is the same height," this check-point where you were at around 1430, it was at the same height as the check-point at Radisani, can you be any more specific? What kind of height?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Height" means if you have an east-western axis, it is around roughly in this height like the other check-point on the other side was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That would be the height that would be marked on a topographic map?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on these east-western axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, on the next page -- on the previous page, you made notes about beating. And then on the next page, at the top, in the English version, it says the following: "Superiors look away/on." And then: "Some even fire at," and then below that: "Check-point, about 15 MUP reservists." This phrase, "some even fire at," Mr. Hutsch, is that a correct English translation of what you wrote in German?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think so, because there were definitely no police officer who was firing with a pistol or something on these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The phrase that you wrote in German at this point, how would you then translate it into English? What were the superiors doing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were -- they were motivating them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. The superiors were motivating who? Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Motivating them -- motivating the subordinates to do what?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: To beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By "them," you mean the ethnic Albanians lying on the road?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, it says -- you have a quote: "You are terrorists. No combat boots on feet. Men are taken away in police cars, buses, direction Skopje. Fire in Ljuboten becoming silence. MUP back from Ljuboten to Ljubanci." And then below that, it says: "Trucks, buses, direction Ljuboten." What does that last line mean, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that when we left the curve going to the right we saw in the picture, that means going to north in the direction of Ljuboten, we saw that some police officers in Ljuboten entered trucks or small buses and drove in direction of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now, this last note, then, was this the last thing that you wrote in your notebook, then, in the Ljuboten area on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender what has been marked as Exhibit P308.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll make a specific annotation for the record to the effect that we will not formally object at this stage, but we reserve our right to challenge the reliability and truthfulness of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, when you passed through that check-point and began to move towards Ljuboten, were you driving fast?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were driving very, very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were afraid that somebody might think we are coming in a combat purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so, again, driving slowly was sort of a safety mechanism?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was also the reason why around 500 metres south of the entrance of Ljuboten we left the car, the Macedonian interpreter and me, and we started to go in front of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Walking?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to what is tab 21 in your binder, and this item, again, comes from 65 ter number 176. It has ERN number N001-7284. Mr. Hutsch, do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says at the top: "PP7 - Sunday, 12 August 2001," and to the right, "Afternoon." Did you make the annotations on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Let's start, first of all, on the left side of the photograph. And, again, perhaps with the usher's assistance, could you take up the pen that's attached to the computer and indicate, either on the photograph or above the photograph, where that check-point was that you passed through a bit after 1430?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's outside this picture in this direction. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And to the left of that arrow, could you write the number "1," please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see the number "1" in red ink in the upper left part of the photograph. Now, we see a blue circle on the left-hand side of the photograph with a smaller blue circle inside it, and then an object next to the blue circle, the smaller blue circle, and then an arrow pointing to some information. Can you explain what you were indicating there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means roughly behind -- north behind the cemetery, there was, in my eyes, an assembly area where some police officers were waiting, and there were also APC. I think, it's a BTR-80 was placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know that these persons were police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflaged uniforms with police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we move -- and you saw this, according to the annotation here, at around 1500 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Moving toward the right, please, going in a westerly direction, would it be fair to say, then, that you and your colleagues were moving slowly up the road to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Towards the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to the left of what we see as the minarets of the mosque, we see a red circle. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. There's an arrow, a red arrow, pointing down, and then we see the words: "Two dead men around 1530." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What do you recall about these two dead men? Were they far apart from each other, close to each other when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were close to each other on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in civilian clothes. As far as I remember, the younger man was wearing a rust brown shirt and some jeans, without shoes. The older man was wearing a black or a dark blue leather jacket and normal dark trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so we don't -- I need to ask a technical question. If this image were marked for identification now and the Prosecution then showed the witness another item, would we then be able to come back to this image and continue to annotate it or would the image then be frozen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would have to be dealt with separately on each occasion as a separate exhibit, Mr. Saxon. Otherwise, we lose the electronic image.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then what I will try to do is forego further annotations. And could this image, as it is marked right now, be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P318, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could, Mr. Hutsch, to what is tab 26 in your binder, and this is Prosecution Exhibit P00019.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps the photo could be enlarged just a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see a body lying off the road. Do you recognise that body?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the man I saw laying on the street, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, then, when you saw this body on the 12th of August, it was laying in the street?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was laying in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could we ask the usher's assistance, please, if you could take up the magic pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Hutsch, if simply draw a simple stick figure to indicate where in the street you saw this person lying on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also indicated, when you saw -- on this afternoon of the 12th of August, you saw two bodies?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you indicate on this photograph -- first of all, the two bodies, would it be possible to draw on this photograph to indicate where the second body was?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, nearly; not completely, but nearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Roughly, could you indicate with the -- let's go a little bit slower. At the feet of this stick figure that you just drew indicating where the first body was laying on the 12th of August, could you write the number "1," please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, could you draw roughly where you saw the second body lying on the road?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] So the head of this man was a little bit more there [Indicates], to the outskirt of the blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could you write the number "2" at what would be the feet of that stick figure you just drew to indicate the second body?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, on that afternoon of the 12th of August, when you an approached these bodies, did you see anything else lying in the road?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rounds of Kalashnikov ammunition in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "rounds of Kalashnikov ammunition," do you mean live rounds or do you mean expended rounds?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Expended rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so are you referring to what's called a shell casing?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you draw, please, roughly -- first of all, were these shell casings, were they all at the very same time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were more like a half circle around these two bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Literally around these two bodies; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Literal --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You just said the shell casings were in a half circle around the two bodies?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were the shell casings right next to the bodies, or were they far away? What distance was there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think between three metres and ten metres, all in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you draw, then, an arrow with that pen, an arrow going toward the left outside the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And draw an arc, please, indicating if that's what it was, of shell casings.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And above the arc, could you write the number "3," please, to indicate where --

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you erase that "3", please. When I said "above the arc," I meant literally above it on the left-hand margin of the page.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here? [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. I meant above the arc, not the arrow.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, the arc, yeah. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So now we see a "3" to indicate this arc of expended shell casings. Now, you had started to draw an arrow off that line. Could you extend that red line, please, towards the position of where the bodies were?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And beneath that red line, could you write "3-10" to indicate three to ten metres.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At that time, when you approached these bodies, did you see any shell casings closer to the bodies?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were single shell cases closer. I think there is also one that you can see in the blood here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't know what you're indicating. Could you draw a small circle around a shell casing that you see?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Could you write the letter "4" beneath that circle?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And was there only one shell casing that you saw closer to their bodies or were there more than one?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I don't remember if there were some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Fine. Your Honours, at this point I would seek to tender this item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P319, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just for clarification, since this session began a bit after 11.00, can the Prosecution continue until around a quarter to 1:00 or does the Chamber prefer to break sooner?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The difficulty is that the last session becomes quite short. It's less strain on the witness and, for that matter, everybody if we keep the periods a little more even. So we would contemplate not long after half past, but at a time that, as usual, fits in with what you were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn now to what is tab 27 in your binder, Mr. Hutsch, and this is Prosecution number P00186. Do you see this photograph, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the old man that was laying in the street on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can refer back to Exhibit -- what was received as Exhibit P319, the previous photograph that you looked at, this would have been Body number 2 in that photograph, right, the second stick figure?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you happen to see this same body a couple of days later on the 14th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this body on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was this body at the same place where you saw it on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was in the entrance of a house, of a farmhouse, south of the place where I saw him on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this would be a convenient time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now. Could I indicate, Mr. Saxon, that in the last session, we will need to conclude the evidence a little short of a quarter to 2:00, to enable the submission which Mr. Apostolski wishes to make, to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Does that mean that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would think about 1.40, ending evidence then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at 1.00. Sorry. Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you allow me 20 minutes for my presentation? So if my learned colleague would be able to finish at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, if not today, tomorrow we will try to fit you in for ten minutes, not 20. You'll have to look at it, again, overnight and get it much shorter. It's merely a reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, so that it is now clear, today you go through to 1.45, no longer 1.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we have the Court Officer's assistance, please, by bringing up, again, what has been marked for identification as Exhibit P318, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is at tab 21, again, of your binder, Mr. Hutsch, if you want to look at the hard copy. Mr. Hutsch, we return to this annotated panoramic photograph, and you see, moving from the left side of the photograph towards the right, toward the mosque, we see this red circle with an arrow pointing to two dead men around 1530 hours. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this reference, is that in relation to the two dead persons that you saw before the break in the photographs?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after you saw these two dead persons, did you continue to walk through Ljuboten, going from east towards west?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see, then, on the other side of the mosque, we see a blue circle and an arrow pointing up, and it says: "Police officers waiting assembly," and this is at around 1545. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, first of all, how did you know that these persons waiting at this spot at this time were police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflaged uniforms with police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, approximately, how many police officers did you see in this area?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe their mood?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in a good mood. The first that what was astonishing me is that they were really in a good discipline. If you compared the normal mood with these reservist police officers or with police officers in common, then most of them at the check-points, they were drinking beer, they were in the afternoon very often drunken, and there were a lot of danger coming out -- getting out from them. These officers, they didn't do nothing in this -- in this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, can I stop you. You said that this group of police officers were in a good mood. How did you know at the time that this group of police officers -- that these officers were in a good mood?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They showed us, for example, the victory sign, the victory sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I can just interrupt, just for the record, the witness is making a "V" signal with his two fingers. So the police officers showed the "V" for victory sign with their hands. Was there anything else that you noticed about them that indicated their mood?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. For example, they said, "Yea, we won against the terrorists," something like that, shouted, and my interpreter translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were still walking outside your vehicle at this time; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we move further towards the west, that is, towards the center of this photograph, we see a blue line with an arrow pointing down, saying: "Around 1600, small groups of police officers (two to three) walking towards the mosque." How did you know these persons were police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were as well wearing camouflaged uniforms with -- with the police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then did you continue again moving from the east towards the west?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see now in the center of the photograph, we see a blue circle and then an arrow pointing down, and it says: "Around 1615, meeting with Johan Tarculovski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So let's just go a bit more slowly now. What did you do, what did you see, at around 1615 that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two white Cherokee police Jeeps coming from the western part of Ljuboten at this T-junction there, and the windows of these cars have been down. And so my interpreter just waved and, yeah, and then we were asked what we are doing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say these were two white police Jeeps. How did you know they were police Jeeps?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the blue lights on the top of their roof, the police "ZZ" badges on the Jeep, and as well their license plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that, "We were asked what we are doing there." Who asked you that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Mr. Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where was Mr. Tarculovski at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was sitting on the seat right to the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that what we call the passenger seat, the front passenger seat?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know that this person was Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met in -- I have to say we were introduced in the beginning, in the first half of March, in Tetovo area by another police commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And let's go to that time in March, if you will. You said you were in the Tetovo area. How is it that you happened to be introduced to Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why he was there or what his function was, but it was a -- it was nearly impossible for me to come close to the positions of the police and especially to the special unit, police unit, the Tigers; and then the hotel manager of the hotel I stayed in introduced me to Goran Skladovski, who was, as far as I know, the commander of the Tigers. And after we have had some coffees together, he promised to bring me close to the position of the police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when this gentleman, Goran Slavkoski, made this offer to you, what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He brought me in his vehicle, in his Jeep, to the -- to a position in the, I would say, ethnical Macedonian quarter of Tetovo where the police positions have been, and there I saw Mr. Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you introduced to Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall at this time, in Tetovo in March of 2001, how Mr. Tarculovski was dressed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dressed in a police uniform, in a camouflaged police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you have any discussions or do anything with Mr. Tarculovski at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just that he was -- or it seems to me that he was giving the orders to the policemen and to the civilians who was fighting there against NLA who was sitting on the Kale mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you said the NLA was sitting on the - I can't see the word - mountain. What do you mean by "the NLA was sitting there"? Can you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA occupied the fortress over Tetovo, and that is called the "Kale," K-a-l-e written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After that initial -- actually, let me go a bit more slowly, please, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could move away from what was marked for identification as Exhibit 318 for a moment. I'll come back to it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As a journalist, do you keep or maintain a database of your contacts?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I'd like to make a brief oral motion to the Chamber. During the proofing sessions of this witness, this witness said he could probably provide some more information that he had stored in his records in Germany to the Office of the Prosecutor. Last weekend, when the witness returned to Germany, he found some additional information and he forwarded it to the Court Officer, and the Court Officer forwarded this information to the Prosecution on Monday. The Prosecution has provided copies of the original German version, as well as translation in English and in Macedonian. What this document is is a note from the records of this witness relating to when he -- when the witness met Mr. Tarculovski. Obviously, since the Prosecution only received this material on Monday, it is not on the Prosecution's first amended exhibit list. However, we make an application at this time for permission to add it to the list. We can provide copies to the Chamber, so that I can discuss this material with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps very briefly. We received this document as well from the Prosecutor both in English and in German. We won't take a position at this stage as to whether it's proper for the Prosecution to add this document to its list. We will keep our objection, if any, to the point where the Prosecution will seek to tender it, if allowed to add it to the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence counsel, Tarculovski, attitude is similar to what my learned friend already presented, although we would like to see the whole notebook that serves the purpose of information source that belongs to the witness, so that we object just this exhibit to be tendered into evidence as a part of his records of some kind, where one cannot clearly see where it originates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, but following on the comment of my colleague, Mr. Apostolski, I would like to indicate perhaps for the Trial Chamber that we had, indeed, sought to obtain the notebooks of Mr. Hutsch through the Prosecution and that the request was made to that effect on our behalf, and that Mr. Hutsch refused to provide these documents to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything further, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, the Chamber is of the view that it should not be at the moment added to your exhibit list, and so that it may not be the subject of specific questioning. You certainly can continue to question the witness about the event that may or may not be described in this notebook, as you have been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, after your first contact with Johan Tarculovski in the Tetovo area in March of 2001, did you see him after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him a couple of times in the -- in the circle of the President of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That was Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall ever seeing Mr. Tarculovski with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not -- no, not with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can return now to the afternoon of the 12th of August, when you saw Mr. Tarculovski inside this Jeep Cherokee, can you recall how Mr. Tarculovski was dressed at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a black overall with police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And about how close were you to Mr. Tarculovski when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably one metre away from the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you see whether Mr. Tarculovski was carrying a weapon or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was wearing a leg holster with a Glock pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A Glock is a brand name of a pistol, an automatic pistol?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the factory that produces in Austria.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall what you observed, if anything, about Mr. Tarculovski's mood at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a good mood, like, yeah, he won something in that the skirmish in Ljuboten, so that he was professional, polite, in a good way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall anything that he said -- do you recall anything that Mr. Tarculovski said at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that what he told my interpreter, and, yeah, he told him that they -- the terrorists now had gone from Ljuboten, that they were defeated, and that everything is under control of the police now in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, at that time Mr. Tarculovski was in a vehicle, in a Jeep; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How many other persons were in that Jeep?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was there just a single police Jeep on that road at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a second one behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what observations, if any, did you make about Mr. Tarculovski's relationship with the other persons in the vehicle or in the other Jeep?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it was clear that he was giving the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, well, can you be a little bit more specific?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, for example --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just, Mr. Hutsch, remember we have to be concerned about the interpreters, because they have the hardest job here, so we need to go more slowly. Why was it clear to you that Mr. Tarculovski was "giving the orders," as you put it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told the driver to stop or to go, and, yeah, he also afterwards, when he went in the direction of Ljuboten, he were giving also orders to other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you observe how the other policemen reacted to the orders of Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was there a person in the back seat of the Jeep where Mr. Tarculovski was riding?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what this person was doing, what role this person had?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my conclusion, what I supposed what was the mission of this person as well as the following crew in this second Jeep, was that they were a kind of protection team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Protection team for whom?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Mr. Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could ask the Court Officer's assistance, please, to move back to what has been marked as identification as Exhibit P318.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you see the annotated photograph again in front of you, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, to the right of the center, we see that blue circle again and your notes around 1615: "Meeting with Johan Tarculovski." After that meeting ended, did you continue to walk up the road towards the west?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you tell us where the two police Jeeps went or in what direction?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went in -- they went in the direction of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So towards the east?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Moving further to the right on this photograph, we see, above the -- first of all, we see a blue circle and an arrow pointing up. It says: "Around 1630, temporary CP," or check-point, "we couldn't pass. Police officers assembling and waiting." So if I understand this circle and the notes that are on this photograph, this blue circle towards the right-hand portion of it represent the furthest westerly point that you and your colleagues reached that afternoon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You noted here: "Police officers assembling." How did you know the persons here were police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflaged uniforms as well as black overall uniforms with police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you see anyone at this spot that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met another police officer who seems to me to be a commander; and in this time, I just knew his pre-name [sic], and that was Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This gentleman who you knew by the name Goran, how did you know who this person was and that his first name was Goran?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the protection team of the Prime Minister of Macedonia; and, in this function, I saw him several times, and it was told to me by the Macedonian interpreter that his pre-name is Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say it was told to you by the Macedonian interpreter that this gentleman's name was Goran, are you speaking about information you received on the 12th of August or information you received when you saw this person as a bodyguard of the Prime Minister?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw him as a bodyguard of the Prime Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can you estimate how many times you had seen Goran in his position as a bodyguard prior to the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe physically what Goran looked like at the time? Is he a big man, small man, medium?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Medium man, very sportive man, a long face -- or a longer face, very short hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you recall, at this check-point on the 12th of August, what language you spoke or you and your colleagues spoke to him in?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke in a mixture of English and Macedonian with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How was this gentleman who you knew to be named Goran dressed on the 12th of August, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dressed with black overall with police badges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did Goran have anything on his hands?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing black handcuffs, but he cut off his fingers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You use the term "handcuffs" --

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not handcuffs, gloves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Gloves with cut fingers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did he wear any kind of protection?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a bulletproof vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall if Goran was carrying any weapons that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I saw, as well, he was wearing a leg holster with a Glock inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did Goran -- the gentleman you knew as Goran say to you and your colleagues when you saw him at the check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stopped us there and he told us that we not could go further because the Minister was there, and it was impossible for us to go past this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what observations did you make about the relationship between this man named Goran and the other police officers who were around that check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he was giving the commands; for example, he told them to put their equipment together, to look after their weapons, and, yeah, also that they shouldn't hang around, that they were just in a disciplined way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you use the word "he," you're referring to this man you knew as Goran?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how did the other police officers respond to Goran's orders?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They paid a lot of respect to him, and they did what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, subsequently, after the events in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, did you learn what the last name or the surname was of this man named Goran?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, I learned that his full name is Goran Stojkov.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall what role you saw Goran Stojkov in after the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I had to return to Macedonia as an officer in -- German Army officer in the German embassy, he was the commander of the police unit or paramilitary unit, the Lions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you ever see Mr. Stojkov, Goran Stojkov, and the Lions together?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them in Skopje itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were they doing in Skopje or what was Mr. Stojkov doing when you sam him?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was just walking the streets in Skopje, because in October, when the Lions were on the street in Skopje, they were doing a kind of patrolling there in the streets in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you saw Mr. Stojkov as well?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After this discussion with the man who at that time you knew as Goran, at this check-point at around 1630, you were told you couldn't go through the check-point, what did you and your colleagues do then?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We decided to leave Ljuboten the way that we came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So does that mean, then, you turned around and you followed the same road back from west to east?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we went to the east to leave the village with the street that is going to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there is -- on the left-hand side of the photograph, there is a small red circle; and underneath that, we see the annotation: "Seen one dead man. People told us three dead men then around 1700." Can you describe what you were referring to there, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were stopped by an old Albanian man with his pre-name Qane, and he stopped us there to bring us up because in that hill he said that there were three dead men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at that time and in that area, did you observe another dead body?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. From the house on, we saw one dead body with -- from the point we were staying, from downstairs, that were laying in this hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender what has been marked for identification Exhibit P318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P318.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hutsch, if you could turn in your binder, please, to what is tab 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could actually see what should be the next photograph in this series with ERN number N -- actually, I can be more specific than that. Yes, this is Exhibit P203.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you recognise what you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the body we saw. But when we saw him, he was laying on his stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And after you saw this body, did you leave Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we leave these events, I want to go back to the period when you were at the check-point with the gentleman who you knew as Goran late that afternoon. You mentioned that the gentleman who you knew as Goran was wearing a bulletproof vest. Do you recall the colour of the vest?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: His vest, it was more modern. I think it was a black one, while his police officers were wearing blue bulletproof vests that were, I would say, the first generation of bulletproof vests.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So after you spoke with the gentleman who you identified as Qane, and you saw the body that we see in Exhibit P203, you left Ljuboten. Did you go to Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did you do that evening?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first what I did is I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. Mr. Hutsch. Maybe -- I'm sorry. My question needs to be more specific. Did you have dinner that evening?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had dinner this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the Dal Met Fu. That is in the center of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a restaurant and a hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you entered that restaurant, did you see anyone who you recognised?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the former Minister of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was Ljube Boskoski alone in that restaurant or was he with other people?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was together with another man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you describe what the other gentleman looked like, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a small man and, yeah, a very strong man with a round face.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This gentleman who you saw with Mr. Boskoski, at that time, did you know this gentleman's name?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Subsequently, later on, did you learn this gentleman's name or some other identity, nickname, or whatever?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In December 2006, I got an information in connection with another man, that the nickname of this man is Bucuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Around --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps before we move on, will the Prosecution ask the witness who this information came from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us or are you willing to tell the Chamber who provided you with this information regarding the nickname Bucuk?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not willing to give this name, but I can give the connection in which this name played a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before you go on, I might leave it -- I might inquire with my colleagues of the Defence, do my colleagues in the Defence wish me to inquire further?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think quite frankly we're going to ask a question to the witness about this, and the process should be -- to the extent that the Prosecution intends to rely on any of that evidence, Mr. Hutsch should be asked who that source is, the name of that source, the position of that person, and any information that would allow an identification of this person who allegedly gave him that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I'll take a minute or two, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, you mentioned that you could describe the connection -- a connection in how you obtained this nickname. Can you describe what you mean by that connection, please, or the context?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I just received information that this man is linked to another man who is probably the member of organised crime in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you receive this information in your work as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. Would this be the appropriate time to stop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
